Name: rewriter_trained_against_one_reader_matched_cost
Title: A Rewriter Learned Against One Reader Is That Reader's: Net-Point Transfer of Execution-Trained Experience Rewriters Across Scaffold, Capability and Backbone, Against Self-Collection at Equal GPU-Hours
Short Hypothesis: An experience rewriter trained by execution-feedback rejection sampling against one reader is that reader's: moved to a different 32B backbone at matched k=0 success it loses at least half of its increment over token-matched verbatim injection (at least 6 net points), moved to the same backbone under a different scaffold it keeps the increment within 6 net, and moved to the same backbone in thinking mode it loses less than the backbone swap does, so reader specificity follows policy proximity rather than capability; and for the held-out backbone, the rewriter's training GPU-hours spent on collecting that backbone's own bank buy at least as much success (non-inferior at 5 net) as importing the foreign-trained rewriter.
Related Work: Model-aware skill alignment (2605.30723) trains a lightweight rewriter per backbone and reports that skills must be adapted to each backbone, but never applies a rewriter trained against one backbone to another, never reports how much of the gain is retained, and does not cost the evolution search against self-collection. SkillRevise (2606.01139) claims revised skills carry generalized procedural knowledge that transfers across models, the opposite prediction, without quantifying what is retained or a matched-cost comparison. CLEAR (2604.07487) trains a context augmentation model by contrastive reflection, SFT and RL against one execution agent and does not test another. AdaCoM (2605.30785) finds the right compression level for a frozen agent's own context depends on that agent's baseline strength, a hint that context artifacts are reader-specific, but it is not a foreign-experience rewriter and reports no held-out reader. HarnessDev (2609.01437) reports self-built harnesses transfer poorly across models. In the home literature, prompt transfer across model sizes has a transferability metric (PANDA 2208.10160) and MePO (2505.09930) claims model-agnostic prompt merits; the question of whether an execution-grounded rewriter is model-agnostic is open. Archived closer_beats_stronger concerned raw memory transfer, not a learned transfer component, and did not separate proximity from capability.
Abstract: Learned transfer components (rewriters, context augmentation models, memory composers) are trained against one consumer and assumed to serve others. We measure, in net success points with cluster-bootstrap CIs, how much of a rewriter's increment survives a change of reader, with the reader manipulated along three separated axes. Two rewriters, both QLoRA adapters on Qwen3-32B trained on equal-size pair sets, are learned on ALFWorld training games by rejection sampling: candidate rewrites of k=3 items retrieved from one shared store (expert, EXAONE-4.0-32B and Qwen3-32B banks) are executed by the in-loop reader, and rewrites that turn a verbatim failure into a success are kept as SFT targets; R_A is trained against Qwen3-32B under the standard scaffold, R_B against EXAONE-4.0-32B. Each rewriter is evaluated on four readers: its training reader, the same backbone under a plan-then-act scaffold (proximity at fixed capability), the same backbone in thinking mode with the budget tuned so k=0 sits 8-12 net above the standard reader (capability at fixed backbone, with a ceiling guard), and the other backbone at verified matched k=0 (backbone). Comparators on every reader are verbatim injection at matched consumer tokens (C_vtok, the smallest k whose tokens cover the rewriter's plan), a training-free prompted rewriter at three decoding budgets, a no-execution-filter adapter, the rewriter given no item (memory-absent) or wrong-type items (mismatched), and for the held-out backbone its own bank enlarged by the episode-equivalent of the rewriter's training GPU-hours. The increment I(R,r) = S(r,R) - S(r,C_vtok) and its differences across readers are the estimands; the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader is reported alongside. Gate 0 requires I(R_A,A) and I(R_B,B) >= 10 net at 274 games x 8 seeds. Every margin is a pre-registered absolute net-point threshold at or above the half-width of the cells that carry it (5 net for within-reader contrasts at 8 seeds, 6 net for cross-reader contrasts), with the fractional readings (half, two thirds of the Gate-0 increment) applied as floors, and the matched-cost claim is a non-inferiority test. The claims fail if the foreign-trained rewriter is within 5 net of the reader-trained one on either reader, if the thinking-mode reader loses more than the other backbone, if the memory-absent rewriter keeps most of the gain, or if the imported rewriter beats equal-cost self-collection by 5 net.
Experiments:
- Store: S = W_exp (expert) + W_EXA (EXAONE-4.0-32B successes, one pass over the 3,553 training games) + W_QW (Qwen3-32B successes, one pass at the same episode budget), the same store read by every reader and used for all rewriter training; W_QW-only and W_EXA-only cells are the self-pool and writer-specific cells; W_EXA+ (matched-cost bank) is extra EXAONE collection whose episode count is fixed before any B cell as R_A's logged training GPU-hours x the measured EXAONE episodes/GPU-h (expected ~4.8 GPU-h x 1,200 = ~5,800 episodes).
- Readers: A Qwen3-32B standard ReAct scaffold, non-thinking, T=0; A' Qwen3-32B plan-then-act scaffold, T=0 (proximity; verify k=0 within +/-5 net of A); A'' Qwen3-32B thinking mode, thinking budget tuned on the C0 cell so k=0 sits 8-12 net above A (capability at fixed backbone; ceiling guard: no A'' cell may exceed 85% success, else the budget is lowered and the cell rerun); B EXAONE-4.0-32B standard scaffold (verify k=0 within +/-5 net of A; if not, B is reported as a joint backbone-and-capability change and P2a/P2b are restated with A'' as the only capability reader). gpt-oss-120b is dropped: it carried no prediction.
- Rewriter training: 1,000 training games; 3 candidate rewrites per game from the prompted Qwen3-32B rewriter R_0 at T=0.8 (input: task, first observation, k=3 items from S; output: one plan in the reader's action format); each candidate and the verbatim k=3 context executed by the in-loop reader (4,000 episodes, ~3.3 GPU-h at 20/min); keep rewrites where the reader succeeded and verbatim failed plus a 1:1 share of success-success pairs; the R_A and R_B pair sets are subsampled to equal size; QLoRA r=32, one epoch (~1.5 GPU-h). Same recipe for R_B with B in the loop; rewriter backbone Qwen3-32B for both so only the in-loop reader differs. R_nf (no filter): the same adapter recipe on one random candidate per game from R_A's candidate set, same pair count (no execution, ~1.5 GPU-h).
- C_vtok rule: verbatim injection from S at the smallest k whose consumer tokens are >= the rewriter's median plan length (expected k=1: +9.1 over static3 in Measurement C; k=3 is +17.2, k=7 is +19.5).
- Cells (274 games x seeds): reader A: C0 (2), C_static = static3 (4), C_v3 (4), C_vtok (8), C_RA (8), C_RB (8), C_Rnf (4), C_R0g prompted rewriter greedy (8), C_R0s prompted rewriter one T=0.8 sample (4), C_R0b3 three T=0.8 samples chosen by a self-selection prompt (4), C_RA_empty task and no item (8), C_RA_mis wrong-type items planted at 3/3 (4), C_self W_QW-only k=3 (4), C_v3[W_EXA] (8), C_RA[W_EXA] (8) = 86 seed-cells, 23.6k episodes. Reader A': C0 (2), C_static (4), C_vtok (8), C_RA (8) = 22, 6.0k. Reader A'': C0 plus budget tuning (4), C_static (4), C_vtok (8), C_RA (8) = 24, 6.6k at ~10/min. Reader B: C0 (2), C_static (4), C_v3 (4), C_vtok (8), C_RA (8), C_RB (8), C_Rnf (4), C_selfcost = S + W_EXA+ verbatim at k=3 (8) and at k=7 (4), C_half = S with W_EXA halved at k=3 (2, bank-size slope), C_v3[W_EXA] (4), C_v3[W_QW] (4), C_RB[W_QW] (4) = 64, 17.5k. Total ~53.7k evaluation episodes, ~50 GPU-h; training ~11 GPU-h (two in-loop rewriters, one no-filter adapter); collection ~11 GPU-h (W_QW, W_EXA, W_EXA+); ~72 GPU-h on two A100s = ~36 h packed, about 3 days with serving changes.
- Estimands: g(r,cond) = S(r,cond) - S(r,C_static); I(R,r) = S(r,R) - S(r,C_vtok) (the adaptation step against direct injection at matched tokens); reader-specificity differences D_B = S(B,C_RB) - S(B,C_RA) and D_A = S(A,C_RA) - S(A,C_RB); transfer losses I(R_A,A) - I(R_A,r) for r in A', A'', B, with the fraction I(R_A,r)/I(R_A,A) reported with joint-bootstrap CIs but never used as a threshold; retained-gain ratio per writer x reader (g(A,C_v3[W_EXA]) / g(B,C_v3[W_EXA]) and its rewritten counterpart g(A,C_RA[W_EXA]) / g(B,C_v3[W_EXA]); g(B,C_v3[W_QW]) / g(A,C_self) and g(B,C_RB[W_QW]) / g(A,C_self) likewise); consumer tokens per episode (rewriter output counted) and episodes/min; training GPU-hours per rewriter.
- Gate 0: I(R_A,A) >= 10 net with lower 95% bound > 0 and I(R_B,B) >= 10 net likewise, at 274 x 8 seeds, before any held-out cell. With C_vtok = k1 this asks the rewriter's ~300-token plan to reach the k=7 verbatim level (+19.5 over static3) at about one fifth of the consumer tokens. A rewriter with 5 <= I < 10 runs the same cells with the absolute margins but the fractional readings are reported as underpowered; I < 5 is reported as a null and R_0 (greedy) becomes the transferred subject for P2 and P4 only.
- Order: C_static and C_R0g on A first; then R_A training and Gate 0; then B, A', A'' cells; the matched-cost and W_EXA/W_QW cells last.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Cheapest first: C_static (static3, the Measurement-C best static arm), then C_R0g (prompted rewriter, no training) before any trained cell.
- Direct injection of the unmodified items at matched consumer tokens (C_vtok) is the comparator inside every increment; C_v3 and, for B, k=7 are reported as the information-matched and best-verbatim comparators, so the rewriter is scored against both fewer tokens and more information.
- Self-pool control at matched collection cost: C_self (W_QW-only, one pass at W_EXA's episode budget) for A, C_v3[W_EXA] for B; C_selfcost converts R_A's logged training GPU-hours into EXAONE episodes at the measured rate and is read at k=3 (primary, the rewriter's own item count) and k=7 (secondary, best k in Measurement C); C_half gives the bank-size slope so a flat curve is visible rather than assumed.
- Memory-absent (C_RA_empty), matched (training reader) and mismatched (C_RA_mis, wrong-type items planted at 3/3, the rewriter analogue of Measurement C's blind1 placebo; and the held-out readers) evaluation of each trained component.
- Prompted rewriter at three budgets (greedy; one T=0.8 sample, the distribution R_A was distilled from; best-of-3 T=0.8 samples chosen by a self-selection prompt at 3x rewriter tokens) so that P5 is not decided by decoding.
- Mechanism ablation: R_nf, the same adapter recipe with no execution filter, scored on A and B; if R_nf shows the same D_A and D_B as the filtered rewriters, reader specificity comes from the candidate generator rather than from the in-loop reader and the mechanism claim fails.
- Named reimplementation: the lightweight per-backbone rewriter of 2605.30723 as C_RA/C_RB; SkillRevise-style trace-conditioned revision (2606.01139) is named as the untested alternative trainer.
- Cut from the previous version: the k=1 rewriter and the reader-identity-in-prompt ablations (no prediction depended on them) and the gpt-oss-120b reader.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- Noise conventions: two-cell paired contrasts within one reader at 274 x 8 seeds carry ~+/-4 net (95%), at 4 seeds ~+/-5.7; differences of increments across readers at 8 seeds ~+/-5.7. Every margin below is at or above the half-width of the cells it uses. 'Confirmed' = point estimate at or above the margin and 95% CI excluding 0; 'falsified' = the 95% CI upper bound below the margin (so a no-loss outcome is falsifying and sits outside the CI); in between, indeterminate and reported as such. Ihat is the Gate-0 point estimate of the relevant reader's own rewriter.
- P1 (headline, reader specificity): D_B = S(B,C_RB) - S(B,C_RA) >= M1 and D_A = S(A,C_RA) - S(A,C_RB) >= M1, M1 = max(5 net, Ihat/2), each with CI excluding 0 (with Ihat = 10 the foreign-trained rewriter retains less than half). C_vtok cancels in both differences; P1 is a two-cell paired contrast at 8 seeds (+/-4), and the test against token-matched verbatim is Gate 0, not P1. Falsifier: either D has upper bound below M1, i.e. the rewrites are reader-agnostic cleaning; the arm can produce it because both rewriters are trained on the same store, the same candidate generator, equal pair counts and the same backbone, differing only in the in-loop reader.
- P2a (backbone swap loses at least half, and more than the scaffold change): I(R_A,A) - I(R_A,B) >= max(6, Ihat/2) and I(R_A,A') - I(R_A,B) >= 6 net, each with CI excluding 0 (A' and B are both verified within +/-5 net of A at k=0, so headroom is matched by construction). Falsifier: either upper bound below its margin (the backbone swap keeps the increment, or the scaffold change costs as much transfer as the backbone change). Arm: (A,C_RA),(A,C_vtok),(A',C_RA),(A',C_vtok),(B,C_RA),(B,C_vtok) at 8 seeds.
- P2b (capability loses less than backbone): I(R_A,A'') - I(R_A,B) >= 6 net with CI excluding 0. Falsifier: upper bound below 6 (the capability change at fixed backbone costs at least as much as the backbone swap). The ceiling guard (A'' k=0 only 8-12 above A, no cell above 85%) keeps a ceiling from manufacturing the falsifier, and the same contrast on the unseen split is reported as a second headroom check. Arm: (A'',C_RA),(A'',C_vtok) at 8 seeds against the B cells. The ordering I(R_A,A') > I(R_A,A'') is expected and reported but not tested, because thinking mode changes headroom.
- P2c (a scaffold change alone does not break the rewriter; non-inferiority): one-sided 95% lower bound of I(R_A,A') - I(R_A,A) above -6 net. Falsifier: point estimate at or below -6 with upper bound below 0. Arm: the A and A' increment cells at 8 seeds.
- P3 (not memorized plans): L = S(A,C_RA) - S(A,C_RA_empty) >= M3 = max(5, 2 Ihat/3) with CI excluding 0 (the item-free rewriter keeps at most a third). Falsifier: upper bound of L below M3, the rewriter with no retrieved item keeps most of its gain, in which case the transfer measured is plan transfer and P1/P2 are re-labelled as such. Arm: C_RA_empty at 8 seeds (+/-4); C_RA_mis at 4 seeds reported alongside.
- P4 (matched cost for the held-out backbone; non-inferiority): Delta = S(B,C_selfcost at k=3) - S(B,C_RA) has one-sided 95% lower bound above -5 net (self-collection at the rewriter's training GPU-hours is not worse than importing the rewriter by more than 5). Falsifier: Delta at or below -5 with upper bound below 0, i.e. the imported rewriter beats the same GPU-hours of B's own experience. The W_EXA+ size is fixed from logged GPU-hours before the cells run; the k=7 and C_half cells are reported so a flat bank-size curve is visible. P4 shares g(B,C_RA) with P2: if I(R_A,B) is below 5 the same data confirm both and P4 is reported as entailed by P2, not as independent support; P4 is independent evidence only when I(R_A,B) >= 5. Arm: C_selfcost and (B,C_RA) at 8 seeds.
- P5 (training buys something): S(A,C_RA) minus the best of S(A,C_R0g), S(A,C_R0s), S(A,C_R0b3) >= 5 net with CI excluding 0. Falsifier: upper bound below 5 against the best prompted cell. Arm: C_R0g at 8 seeds, C_R0s and C_R0b3 at 4, against (A,C_RA); taking the maximum is conservative for the claim.
- P6 (the rewriter moves the retained-gain ratio): on the EXAONE-only bank, g(A,C_RA[W_EXA]) - g(A,C_v3[W_EXA]) >= 5 net with CI excluding 0, reported with the ratio g(A,.)/g(B,C_v3[W_EXA]) before and after rewriting (joint bootstrap). Falsifier: upper bound below 5, the rewriter does not move reader A toward the writer's own gain on the writer's bank; this is stronger than Gate 0 because the comparator is k=3 verbatim, not k=1. Arm: C_v3[W_EXA] and C_RA[W_EXA] on A at 8 seeds, C_v3[W_EXA] on B at 4 seeds as the denominator.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired per-game success differences over 274 games x seeds; cluster bootstrap over games with seeds nested (10,000 resamples, percentile 95% CIs; one-sided 95% bounds for the two non-inferiority tests); ratio CIs by joint bootstrap of numerator and denominator; the P1 differences and the cross-reader differences of increments computed per game. Working half-widths from the brief: +/-8 at 274 x 2, +/-5.7 at 274 x 4, +/-4 at 274 x 8 for two-cell paired contrasts; cross-reader differences of increments at 8 seeds ~+/-5.7. All margins are absolute net points at or above these; if a headline cell's measured half-width exceeds its margin, that cell is extended to 12 seeds before the contrast is reported. Gate 0 at 8 seeds before any held-out cell. Multiplicity: P1 (both parts required) is the one confirmatory contrast, P2a/P2b secondary, P2c/P3-P6 exploratory, all reported with CIs and no further correction. Reader and rewriter temperature 0 everywhere at evaluation except the two T=0.8 R_0 cells; A' differs from A by scaffold only (the temperature change was dropped to avoid sampling variance). Headroom guard for A'': thinking budget tuned on the C0 cell so k=0 sits 8-12 net above A; any A'' cell above 85% success is rerun at a lower budget; increments on the unseen split are reported for all readers. Training confounds: R_A and R_B use the same candidate generator, equal pair counts (subsampled to the smaller), the same hyperparameters and seeds; the retained pairs' game-type mix is reported. Consumer tokens per episode include the rewriter's generated plan; training GPU-hours are logged from the runner and converted to EXAONE episodes at the measured rate to fix W_EXA+ before any B cell. GPU plan: during training one A100 serves the in-loop reader and the other the candidate generator; the QLoRA job runs on one GPU while the other serves the first A cells; at evaluation each GPU runs one vLLM replica, Qwen3-32B readers serve the LoRA rewriters on the same replica, and B's replica pairs with the rewriter replica on the other GPU; concurrency tuned to a running queue >= 8 per replica; throughput (episodes/min) logged per cell.
Preprint Collision Check: All queries via tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (s2=ok hf=ok). (1) recent, closest named method: 'model-conditioned skill rewriter adapt skills to target backbone transfer to held-out model' -> 2605.30723 (rewriter per backbone, no held-out reader), SkillRevise 2606.01139 (claims cross-model transfer of revised skills, no fraction reported), 2605.23899, Skill-R1 2605.09359, SkillX 2604.04804; the two nearest cards make opposite predictions and neither reports what is retained by a held-out reader or a matched-cost self-collection arm. (2) recent: 'context augmentation model execution feedback transfer to different execution agent backbone' -> AdaCoM 2605.30785 (verified with s2cli paper; reader-strength-dependent compression for the agent's own context), CLEAR 2604.07487, HarnessDev 2609.01437 (harnesses transfer poorly across models), Harness-Bench 2605.27922; none trains a component against one reader and scores it on another. (3) home: 'prompt optimization transferability across target language models optimized on one model evaluated on another' (answered after a rate-limit delay by the same channel) -> MePO 2505.09930 (model-agnostic prompt merits), PANDA 2208.10160 (prompt transfer across model sizes with a transferability metric), 2305.13954, GReaTer 2412.09722; these ask the home-vocabulary question for static prompts and do not cover execution-grounded rewriting of retrieved trajectories or a self-collection cost arm. (4) recent: 'reconstruct retrieved experience conditioned on current state agent cross-model transfer' -> MemHarness 2607.28272, 2608.26730, 2607.13884; no held-out reader. No paper found that reports how much of a learned rewriter's gain a held-out reader retains with proximity and capability separated.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Rejection sampling may yield only a few hundred contrastive pairs, so an adapter can underfit and miss Gate 0 at 10 net; 5-10 net runs the design with the fractional readings flagged as underpowered, below 5 the prompted rewriter R_0 is the fallback subject for P2 and P4 and P1/P3/P5 are reported as nulls. Gate 0 is demanding by construction: with C_vtok = k1 it asks a ~300-token plan to match k=7 verbatim; if the rewriter's plans turn out longer than one item, C_vtok becomes k=2 and the bar drops accordingly. The rewriter backbone is Qwen3-32B for both R_A and R_B, so on reader A both rewriters share a same-family advantage; this is symmetric within P1 but limits generality across rewriter backbones. B and A'' remain confounded with capability if EXAONE does not land within +/-5 net of A at k=0 or if the thinking budget cannot be tuned into the 8-12 window; the stated fallbacks restrict P2 to the readers that verify. Thinking mode halves throughput (budgeted at 10/min). Cross-reader differences of increments are the least powered contrasts (+/-5.7 at 8 seeds), so P2a/P2b confirm only for effects of 6 net or more. The C_selfcost arm may sit on a flat part of the bank-size curve; C_half and the k=7 cell make that visible and P4 is then reported as 'both null' rather than as support. The store contains each reader's own writer's items alongside foreign ones (the same store is read by every reader, per the round rule), so the writer-specific claims live in the W_EXA-only and W_QW-only cells. ALFWorld's six procedures make the rewriter's job narrow; a second domain is out of budget; no contamination-rate arm beyond the 3/3 wrong-type cell is run.
Addresses gap: G17 (learned transfer components not tested on held-out backbones, capability gaps or scaffolds) as the primary target; G20 (adaptation cost never matched against plain retrieval or self-collection) through C_vtok and C_selfcost; G18 through the retained-gain ratio under the rewriter.
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: the in-scope list names a model-conditioned skill rewriter (2605.30723) as a baseline to reimplement and Q5 asks whether a rewriter learned against one reader transfers; this idea supplies what neither states, the net-point transfer loss per axis as the estimand (fraction reported), its ordering by proximity versus capability with the reader manipulated on three separated axes, and the equal-GPU-hour self-collection comparison for the held-out backbone. Digest card: 2605.30723 claims skills must be adapted per backbone and trains a rewriter per backbone; this idea claims the rewriter itself is reader-specific by a measured net-point loss, that a memory-absent rewriter must not keep the gain, that a no-execution-filter adapter must not show the same specificity, and that importing it does not beat self-collection at equal cost, none of which the card tests; the conflicting card 2606.01139 claims cross-model transfer of revised skills without quantification, and this design arbitrates between them. Archived closer_beats_stronger measured raw memory transfer with proximity and capability confounded; here the transferred object is a trained component and the two axes are separated within one backbone.
Changes made:
- P1: replaced the fraction-of-Gate-0 margin (~2 net) with an absolute margin M1 = max(5, Ihat/2) at 274 x 8 seeds (+/-4) for the four rewriter x reader cells; raised Gate 0 from 6 to 10 net at 8 seeds so 'less than half retained' is 5 net; stated explicitly that C_vtok cancels in P1 and that the verbatim test is Gate 0.
- P2: dropped transfer fractions as thresholds (reported only); replaced with net-point contrasts P2a (backbone loss >= max(6, Ihat/2) and A' vs B >= 6) and P2b (A'' vs B >= 6) with 8 seeds on A', A'', B, plus a TOST P2c at delta = 6 for the scaffold change; A' now differs by scaffold only at T=0; A'' thinking budget tuned to a k=0 window of 8-12 above A with an 85% ceiling guard and an unseen-split check so headroom cannot manufacture the falsifier.
- P3: C_RA_empty moved to 8 seeds; absolute margin max(5, 2 Ihat/3) with the falsifier as an upper-bound test.
- P4: restated as non-inferiority (one-sided 95% bound above -5) with the falsifier as a >= 5 net rewriter advantage; W_EXA+ size fixed from logged GPU-hours before the B cells; added k=7 and half-bank cells so a flat bank-size curve is visible; declared the P2-P4 coupling and when P4 counts as independent.
- P5: C_R0 greedy at 8 seeds plus T=0.8 single-sample and self-selected best-of-3 cells; claim is S(A,C_RA) minus the best prompted cell >= 5 with CI excluding 0.
- P6: added the missing W_EXA-only cells on A (C_v3, C_RA at 8 seeds) and the (B, W_EXA, C_v3) denominator; claim is a 5-net difference against k=3 verbatim, the ratio reported with joint-bootstrap CI.
- Design: one shared store (W_exp + W_EXA + W_QW) read by every reader; equal-size pair sets for R_A and R_B; added the no-filter adapter R_nf as the mechanism ablation; cut the k=1 and reader-identity ablations and the gpt-oss-120b reader; cell-by-cell seed counts and the GPU-hour arithmetic (~53.7k evaluation episodes, ~72 GPU-h, ~3 days on two A100s) stated.
- Kept sharp: the central claim is still that the rewriter is the reader's, now stated as absolute net-point losses that a single 8-seed cell can refute; the fractional language (less than half, two thirds) survives as floors on those margins rather than being softened; the matched-cost claim remains that importing does not win; the proximity-versus-capability ordering is still tested on separated axes; and the no-filter ablation adds a way for the mechanism to fail rather than removing one.
